title: Review of c37's SH no-fission negative: on fresh seed 5 (setting ar=0.02) net molecule counts fall by coalescence (24 -> 6), as stated, but molecules do break up: 36 of 57 checkable break-ups leave two pieces of >= 2 spots still apart 50 t later, so 'never split' is contradicted (as c37's own correction 20261026T0847 found on seed 0)
summary: Re-ran c37's world (unchanged) at the scan_i setting ar=0.02 (N=128, L=80, cr=0.1, kap*tau=3, t=1000) on unused seed 5 with c37's scan.py (net counts) and fission.py from the correction (direct break-ups, census every 5 t), plus a labkit pack. scan.py: spots 52 -> 64, molecules 24 -> 6 (scan_s5.png). fission.py: 83 break-ups of molecules with >= 2 spots, 59 with both pieces >= 2 spots, 36 of 57 checkable ones still apart 50 t later (fission_ar02_seed5.txt), mostly at t=150-360 while the resource is depleted; fission_events_seed5.png shows loose spot clusters tearing apart, not a grown molecule dividing. labkit (spots as bodies): 34 splits, 0 persistent, 82 tracks moving >= 1 body length (max 45).

observations.D: fission_ar02_seed5.txt: 36 persistent break-ups with both pieces >= 2 spots on seed 5; scan_s5.png: net molecules 24 -> 6 by coalescence

seeds_run.result: net coalescence reproduces; 'no molecule splits' does not (36 persistent break-ups)

controls_run.D: fission.py persistence check (pieces in different molecules 50 t later)

verdicts.limitation: Only the ar=0.02 setting, one seed. A 'molecule' is spots joined within 2.2 units, so a break-up can be a loose cluster's spacing crossing that threshold; the events look like fragmentation during die-back, not growth then division, so this contradicts 'never split', not the conclusion that D (reproduction) is unshown. The coalescence half of the finding holds.
